newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels say take key town, closing on Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels say take key town, closing on Kinshasa.

text.p: Zairean rebels said on Monday they had captured the town of Kananga, capital of Western Kasai province and one of the largest towns outside Kinshasa that was still in government hands.
Kananga fell to rebel forces on Saturday, said Voice of the People radio broadcast from the eastern town of Goma, rebel headquarters.
"Kasumbalesa (on the Zambian border) and Kananga were taken by the Alliance on Friday 11 and Saturday 12 respectively," the radio said. There was no independent confirmation.

"The fall of Kananga leaves the Alliance in a good position to move on Bandundu whose people are eagerly awaiting liberation," the radio said. Bandundu is only 270 km (165 miles) northeast of Kinshasa.

Rebels of Laurent Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire fighting to oust president Mobutu Sese Seko have seized control of the eastern half of the vast country in under six months.
The rebels took Zaire's second city Lubumbashi last week, depriving the government of valuable mineral resources.
There was little looting at Kananga, close to the Angolan border, because of the vigilance of inhabitants who welcomed rebels, the radio said.

Zaire government troops, former Rwandan government soldiers and extremist Interahamwe militiamen fled 125 km (78 miles) west to Kananga after their defeat at the diamond capital Mbuji-Mayi, which fell to rebels on April 5, witnesses said.

Rebels of Laurent Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL) said on Sunday they were resuming their offensive after a three-day halt called to give ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko time to resign.
Senior alliance officials said in Mbuji-Mayi last week capturing Kananga would be straightforward because government forces were using the town as a stepping stone as they retreated to Kinshasa.
Its fall would leave rebels 950 km (593 miles) east of Kinshasa on the southern front.
The rebels are using the massive Zaire river to advance through the north of the country and are marching along a southern axis via Mbuji-Mayi and Kananga towards Kikwit and Bandundu.
Rebel forces are just 300 km (187 miles) from an increasingly nervous Kinshasa, according to Voice of the People, which gave no further details.
